title: Time-dependent Berry curvature and quantum metric of Floquet-Bloch states
abstract: The quantum geometry of Bloch bands, characterized by the Berry curvature and the quantum metric, underpins a wide range of linear and nonlinear responses in static systems. Here, we extend this framework to periodically driven (Floquet) systems by introducing a time-dependent Berry curvature and quantum metric defined directly in the Floquet-Bloch basis. We derive optical sum rules that relate the Fourier components of these geometric quantities to the optical conductivity and demonstrate that, under ideal Floquet-band occupations, the first-order DC Hall and longitudinal responses at harmonic frequencies vanish identically. We further introduce a mixed Berry curvature involving time and momentum derivatives, which gives rise to a non-adiabatic quantized charge-pumping mechanism that occurs naturally during each driving period without requiring adiabatic evolution. In addition, we identify the time-domain quantum metric as a measure of the energy fluctuations of a Floquet band and interpret its mixed components as quantifying polarization-energy correlations. A comprehensive symmetry analysis reveals how time-reversal, sublattice (chiral), particle-hole, inversion, rotational, and reflection symmetries constrain the time-dependent quantum geometric tensor and its associated topological invariant. Numerical simulations of the Rudner-Lindner-Berg-Levin model and a fully symmetric Floquet model confirm the analytical predictions. These results establish the time-dependent quantum geometric tensor as a unified framework for describing the geometric, topological, and dynamical properties of periodically driven quantum systems, with direct implications for optical spectroscopy, quantum transport, and topological charge-pumping experiments.
summary: This paper develops a unified theoretical framework using the time-dependent quantum geometric tensor to characterize periodically driven quantum systems. It extends concepts like Berry curvature to the time domain, deriving sum rules that link these geometric quantities directly to measurable optical responses. The findings establish this tensor as a key diagnostic tool for understanding topological and dynamical effects in Floquet matter.
main_problem: The primary goal is extending the concept of quantum geometry (Berry curvature and quantum metric) from static Bloch bands to periodically driven Floquet systems.
main_result: The authors establish a time-dependent quantum geometric tensor as a unified framework describing geometric, topological, and dynamical properties in these driven systems. They show that first-order DC Hall and longitudinal responses vanish under ideal band occupations.
method: The methodology involves defining time-dependent geometric tensors in the Floquet-Bloch basis, deriving optical sum rules relating Fourier components of these tensors to measurable conductivity, and performing detailed symmetry analyses.
model_or_system: The study focuses on two-dimensional (2D) quantum systems subjected to a time-periodic Hamiltonian, analyzed using Floquet theory. Specific models include the Rudner-Lindner-Berg-Levin (RLBL) model and fully symmetric Floquet Hamiltonians.
key_observables: Time-dependent Berry curvature ($\Omega_{xy}(t)$), quantum metric ($g_{xy}(t)$), optical conductivity $\sigma(\omega)$, and quantized charge pumping currents.
important_parameters: Periodicity $T$, quasienergy bands, harmonic frequencies $n\Omega$, and the assumption of ideal Floquet-band occupations.
main_assumptions: The analysis heavily relies on assuming ideal occupation (bands fully filled or empty) to derive zero DC response sum rules. It also assumes orthogonality for the Floquet states.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate time dependence of phase band extrema, components of geometric tensors ($G_{xy}^-, G_{xt}^-$), and confirm analytical predictions regarding conductivity zeros and sum rules.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the time-dependent quantum geometric tensor in Floquet systems to deriving optical sum rules. It then explores non-adiabatic charge pumping via mixed Berry curvature, followed by a comprehensive symmetry analysis constraining the tensor components.
why_interesting: This work provides powerful diagnostic tools (the time-dependent quantum geometric tensor) for understanding how topological and geometric properties manifest in driven quantum matter, which is highly relevant to open quantum systems and Floquet engineering.
